papers.title: A Solar Optical Clock
papers.abstract: Precision spectroscopy underpins quantum sensing, atomic timekeeping, and the search for terrestrial-mass exoplanets. Finding an Earth-Sun analog requires fractional splitting of spectral features that rivals the precision of the best laboratory spectroscopy. This corresponds to resolution of a few parts in $10^5$ of a typical stellar spectral line, or a Doppler velocity precision of less than 10 cm s$^{-1}$. Only a few astrophysical spectrometers reach this regime, and only by dispersing starlight with large gratings and averaging thousands of lines. Here, we show that comparable precision can be achieved on a single solar line by leveraging techniques used in quantum sensors and optical clocks. A laser is frequency-locked to the 1565 nm solar Fe I line by coupling to a single mode of the solar thermal field and counted against an optical frequency comb referenced to the SI second, thus creating a solar optical clock. Operating at the fundamental photon-noise limit of thermal heterodyne spectroscopy, we achieve centroid precision of one part in $10^9$ of the optical frequency, or 30 cm s$^{-1}$ in radial velocity. We recover the Sun's five-minute acoustic oscillations and the expected Rossiter-McLaughlin signal during a solar eclipse. Combining these techniques from quantum sensing with a thirty-meter-class telescope could enable our demonstrated precision on the nearest Sun-like stars in a few hours. Multiplexing such absolute frequency measurements across lines with different magnetic sensitivity and formation depth would reduce averaging time and help disentangle stellar granulation and activity from the Doppler signature of terrestrial exoplanets, providing new approaches to address some of the most demanding measurements in astrophysical spectroscopy.

papers.title: The "Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery" Workshop: A Community Roadmap for the Future of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory After the LSST
papers.abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory will complete its ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) in the mid-2030s. Its 8.4 m aperture and 9.6 square degree field of view give it an \'etendue unmatched by any facility planned for that era. The Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery workshop (KIPAC/SLAC, 3-5 August 2026) brought together approximately 100 participants to discuss Rubin's future after LSST. This paper summarizes the workshop's structure and discussions across five working groups. The continued-surveying group explored a machine-learning foundation model pretrained on Rubin imaging for detection, deblending, and classification. The cadence group considered allocating post-LSST observing time and strategies for transiting exoplanets, Type Ia supernova cosmology, time-delay cosmography, and second-scale transients. The filter group explored broadband, medium-band, and narrowband filters for photometric redshifts, high-redshift large-scale structure, AGN reverberation mapping, Galactic archaeology, and emission-line imaging. The multi-messenger group explored follow-up of next-generation gravitational-wave and neutrino sources, including standard sirens, kilonovae, and Galactic supernovae. The technology group organized options by cost and lead time, including fast readout, new filters, a faster shutter, and summit edge computing. Cross-cutting topics included AI/ML, Chilean and Latin-American co-leadership, satellite megaconstellations, and weather and climate trends at Cerro Pach\'on. White papers and workshop talks are available through https://zenodo.org/communities/rubin2036workshop/ and https://rubin-observatory.github.io/Rubin-Beyond-LSST/pages/Rubin2036proceedings/.

papers.title: Finite-range hair from a nonlocal matter sector: charged Yukawa black holes
papers.abstract: { We construct a new exact charged, static and spherically symmetric black-hole solution of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with an additional anisotropic matter sector, whose metric is the Reissner--Nordstr\"om geometry endowed with a Yukawa-type contribution. The Yukawa term is exponentially screened: it is visible in the strong-field region but carries no independent asymptotic charge. We obtain an analytic parametrization of the extremal curve, identify the condition for higher-order degenerate horizons, characterize the curvature singularity and establish the weak, null, dominant and strong energy conditions. We further study the horizon thermodynamics, including the conjugate variables associated with the amplitude and range of the Yukawa sector and the corresponding generalized Smarr relation. The photon sphere, shadow, ray-traced appearance and quasinormal ringdown are then analyzed, with quasinormal frequencies computed through the sixth-order WKB expansion and confirmed, overtones included, by an independent spectral method. {Confronting the model shadow with Event Horizon Telescope measurements of M87* and Sgr A* constrains the finite-range sector directly, favoring its strongly screened, near-Reissner--Nordstr\"om regime.} This provides a unified geometric and phenomenological characterization of finite-range charged black-hole hair in ordinary Einstein gravity. }

papers.title: Tight asteroseismic upper limits on hot subdwarf magnetism
papers.abstract: The apparent absence of magnetism in subdwarf B stars (sdBs) has emerged as an outstanding observational puzzle, especially in light of their likely origin in binary interactions. Gravity-mode pulsations in some sdBs offer a unique opportunity to extend recent successes in asteroseismic magnetic field detection in red giants. In the presence of strong magnetic fields, gravity modes are expected to be significantly damped, suppressing their observed amplitudes. We place stringent upper limits on magnetic fields in 30 hot subdwarfs by using the observation of low-frequency dipole and quadrupole modes to rule out magnetic suppression. Even under conservative assumptions, our upper limits constrain near-surface magnetic fields to below a kilogauss in roughly half of our sample, with the strongest individual constraint reaching down to $\sim20\,\mathrm{G}$. These upper limits reinforce the apparent dearth of magnetic fields in hot subdwarfs and demonstrate asteroseismology as a powerful new probe of magnetism in these stars.

papers.title: Magnetic-field dependence of the QCD electric screening mass parameter through $g^4$ in hot and dense matter
papers.abstract: A constant magnetic field modifies the hard electric screening sector of hot and dense QCD and generates a directional splitting at $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$. We determine the strict-hard screening pole through $g^4$ for three massless flavors with physical $u,d,s$ charges, retaining the full $eB/T^2$ dependence without a weak- or strong-field expansion. The shifted-frequency construction used for the two-loop exchange contribution is a background-field Feynman-gauge curvature; we derive and apply its local conversion to the ordinary Feynman-gauge self-energy before assembling the screening pole. The leading magnetic shift is isotropic, while the $g^4$ directional splitting arises from the one-loop anisotropic kinetic normalization; the symmetry-allowed finite-density $A_0F_{12}$ mixing is numerically small over the studied range for physical $u,d,s$ charges. For $\mu/T=0$ and $1$, the magnetic $g^4$ coefficient is positive over $0\le eB/T^2\le4$ and is strongly reduced by density. Extending the calculation to $0\le\mu/T\le2$ at $eB/T^2=1$ and $4$ reveals sign reversals of both the leading magnetic coefficient and the directional splitting at sufficiently large density. The zero-field limit reproduces the Braaten-Nieto result and its finite-density extension by Vuorinen. The running coupling used only for the phenomenological magnetic mass shift is chosen independently of $B$, so that all magnetic-field dependence through $g^4$ resides in the calculated coefficients.

papers.title: Quantum Bianchi IX Anisotropies as Inflationary Relics in the Primordial Spectrum
papers.abstract: Starting from the WheelerDeWitt equation, we investigate whether quantum anisotropies can survive inflation as relics of the preinflationary geometry and leave an imprint on the primordial curvature spectrum. We perform a BornOppenheimer separation of the wave functional into slow gravitational and fast matter components, justified by the hierarchy between the Planck scale and the lower matter scale, associated here with the inflaton. The full wave functional is then treated through a semiclassical WKB expansion in M to the minus 1, where M is quadratic in the Planck mass. The gravitational sector consists of a de Sitter background supplemented by homogeneous quantum anisotropies in the smallanisotropy regime of the Bianchi IX potential, while matter is represented by a single scalar inflaton field. At order M in the expansion parameter, the WheelerDeWitt equation reproduces the vacuum HamiltonJacobi equation with a cosmological constant. At order M to 0, the internal freedom of the BornOppenheimer factorization separates quantum field theory on curved spacetime from the anisotropy dynamics, described by timedependent harmonic oscillators. At order M to the minus 1, we obtain the quantumgravitational correction to matter. The anisotropy wave function enters explicitly the corresponding operator, so the corrected dynamics retains information about the Bianchi IX quantum state. The curvature power spectrum consequently contains two distinguishable contributions: one independent of the anisotropy state and a genuinely anisotropic term. The latter survives through the quantum variance of the anisotropies, thereby identifying the mechanism through which the preinflationary quantum geometry can affect the primordial spectrum.

papers.title: Identifying a jet-shaped point-symmetric morphology in the supernova remnant HB9
papers.abstract: I identify a point-symmetric morphology in the supernova remnant HB9 (G160.9+2.6), supposedly a core-collapse supernova (CCSN) remnant (CCSNR), and attribute this structure to two or more pairs of jets that exploded the star within the jittering-jets explosion mechanism (JJEM). The pairs of jets that shape the point-symmetric morphology of HB9 are part of a larger number of pairs that exploded the star. The point-symmetric structure is composed of a pair of ears, a pair of ears/nozzles, a pair of dents, and a pair of bright bars. Although these pairs of morphological features are small and the point-symmetric structure is subtle, I consider the identification robust. I use visual inspection to identify the point-symmetric morphology of HB9, a method commonly used to identify jet-shaped, point-symmetric morphologies in other astrophysical objects, such as cooling-flow clusters of galaxies and planetary nebulae. I present arguments for jet-driven shaping rather than CSM shaping. These findings support earlier claims that the JJEM is the primary explosion mechanism of CCSNe.

papers.title: Exponential Growth of Turbulent Cross Helicity in Shear-Flow-Driven Turbulence
papers.abstract: Cross helicity, the velocity--magnetic-field correlation, is an ideal invariant of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics and constrains energy cascades and magnetic-field generation. Although cross helicity typically decays via visco-resistive effects, we analytically demonstrate that it grows exponentially in sheared inhomogeneous turbulence. This cross-helical shear instability is confirmed using three-dimensional numerical simulations. Growth requires a nonzero gradient of the Reynolds--Maxwell stress to produce turbulent cross helicity; this production overcomes effective losses when shear exceeds a threshold set by the ratio of turbulent magnetic to momentum diffusivities.

papers.title: Hybrid Stars with Different Amount of Quark Matter
papers.abstract: In a previous work, we explored the possibility of neutron stars with large quark cores. Through Bayesian inference, we obtained large sets of equations of state imposing constraints regarding the properties of nuclear matter, mass-radius data from NICER, the GW170817 data from Virgo-LIGO collaboration, perturbative QCD and causality. We also imposed that the maximum mass neutron star (NS$\text{max}$) must have a large quark core. In this work, we obtain a new set of equations of state (SmallQ set) with the same constraints as before. However, we relaxed the last constraint, imposing only that NS$\text{max}$ must have quark core, regardless of its size. We compare the results with the set from our previous paper constrained by NICER and GW170817 observations NJL-GW. For both sets, we use the Relativistic Mean Field model with nonlinear meson interactions for the hadron phase and the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model with four- and eight-quark interaction terms for the quark phase. The SmallQ set has higher values of phase transition density, with 3 -- 4.5 $\rho_0$, compared to the NJL-GW, with 2 -- 2.5 $\rho_0$. The new set describes NSs with smaller radius and smaller tidal deformability, and is more compatible with NICER and GW170817 data. A difference in the quark matter composition is observed, with a larger quark strange fraction occurring in the SmallQ set. Within this set, $2 M_\odot$ NSs may contain little to no quark matter. It is shown that there is a non negligible fraction of EOS whose mass-radius curve presents a positive slope for 1.8 $M_\odot$ stars, while for nucleonic stars this fraction is negligible and for hyperonic stars the slope is always negative.

papers.title: KMOS Spectroscopic Follow-up of 16 Star Cluster Candidates of the Sagittarius Dwarf Galaxy
papers.abstract: The Sagittarius (Sgr) dwarf spheroidal galaxy hosts several known globular clusters and numerous additional cluster candidates identified toward its crowded central regions. Establishing the nature of these candidates is difficult because apparent spatial and astrometric structure can arise from the underlying Sgr population. We investigate sixteen Minni stellar-cluster candidates with KMOS spectroscopy to determine whether the observed stars are compatible with Sgr and whether any candidate field shows evidence for a distinct stellar system. We analyse H-band KMOS spectra of 341 targets from the VVVX-GalCen Spectroscopic Survey, deriving radial velocities (RVs) and empirical metallicities. We compare these with an independent Sgr spectroscopic sample and use VVVX photometry and Gaia DR3 astrometry to test for localized stellar excesses relative to local control fields. Of the 341 KMOS targets, 256 (75%) have RVs within the adopted Sgr interval, and their metallicities broadly overlap the Sgr comparison population. No field shows statistically compelling kinematic evidence for a distinct system after accounting for the multiple candidates examined. Minni 329 shows the strongest spatial excess, but this is not significant after multiple-testing correction and is not accompanied by significant central concentration. The KMOS targets predominantly trace the Sgr population, but Sgr compatibility alone does not confirm the individual candidates as distinct stellar clusters. None of the sixteen fields can be confirmed as a separate stellar system with the present data, although this does not establish that the original candidates are spurious. Deeper imaging and larger spectroscopic samples are required to determine their physical nature.

papers.title: Geometrically Induced Semiclassical Limit for Quasinormal Modes and Greybody Factors in Higher-Dimensional Near-Ultracold spacetimes
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the correspondence between quasinormal modes (QNMs) and greybody factors (GBFs) in higher-dimensional Reissner--Nordst\"{o}m--de Sitter black holes based on the massless scalar field. Our analysis focuses on the QNMs in the near-ultracold family where the inner, outer, and cosmological horizons are close together. Under the geometric limit condition, the leading-order Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin term of the QNM is dominant for fixed angular quantum numbers and dimensionality without imposing the eikonal limit. Particularly, the corresponding GBFs also retain the explicit form of both parameters. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the half-transmission frequency of the GBF and its derivative are related to null geodesics, in terms of aspects such as the angular frequency and Lyapunov exponent, with the use of both parameters. We provide their relationships in arbitrary dimensionality. Furthermore, the higher-order corrections to the QNMs are investigated at the Nariai limit and in the near-ultracold geometry with separated horizons.

papers.title: Topological ModMax--AdS Black Holes: Extremality, Charge Normalization, and Limits of WGC Diagnostics
papers.abstract: We study four-dimensional topological anti-de Sitter black holes sourced by ModMax electrodynamics and its sign-reversed counterpart. Distinguishing the field-strength amplitude from the conserved displacement flux fixes the charge normalization, potential, and first law. We classify the exact extremal roots for spherical, planar, and hyperbolic horizons; in particular, the hyperbolic ModMax branch has no upper-charge discriminant bound and contains a finite-charge zero-mass point. We also derive the unstable spherical null circular orbit and evaluate the local near-horizon AdS$_2$ Breitenlohner--Freedman index for an explicitly specified charged-scalar probe. These are classical diagnostics, not a WGC verdict: the model does not specify a charged-particle spectrum, an ultraviolet completion, or the global perturbation problem. The distance and de Sitter conjectures cannot be quantitatively tested with the fixed-coupling AdS data considered here.

papers.title: Photometric variability of blue supergiants: Constraints on stellar masses and evolutionary stages
papers.abstract: Blue supergiants (BSGs) are crucial to understanding the evolution of massive stars. Although distinguishing between pre- and post-red supergiant (RSG) phases is challenging, stellar pulsations provide valuable constraints on their masses and evolutionary status. This study analyzes TESS light curves of six BSGs with high L/M to identify periodicities. We performed theoretical modeling of the radial unstable modes to characterize the strange modes. We aim to estimate asteroseismic masses, compare them with spectroscopic and evolutionary mass estimates, and assess the evolutionary stage of the stars. We employed the Lomb-Scargle periodogram and the weighted wavelet Z-transform to address quasiperiodic behavior and time-varying signals. A linear nonadiabatic stability analysis was performed to test for radial perturbations, generating eigenfrequencies that enable stellar mass estimation. In addition, we characterized the stochastic low-frequency variability (SLFV). We derive a first guess at the asteroseismic masses. We find that HD 74371 and HD 79186 are evolving blueward following the RSG phase, while the evolutionary stage of HD 115842 cannot be uniquely determined with the available mass estimates. We also find that HD 52382 and HD 99953 are likely in the post-RSG phase; however, their low masses are difficult to reconcile with the available evolutionary models. The extreme supergiant HD 80077 shows the largest mass discrepancy in the sample, suggesting a more complex evolutionary history. The SLFV properties do not provide a clear diagnostic of the evolutionary stage. These results highlight the potential of asteroseismology as a complementary tool for constraining the evolutionary status of BSGs. However, the mass discrepancies found for some objects indicate that additional observational and theoretical efforts are required.

papers.title: Revisiting the Unknown Unknowns in Transient Astrophysics with the SKA Telescopes
papers.abstract: It was already recognised in the 2004 and 2014 SKA Science Case Chapters: "The Exploration of the Unknown" and "The SKA and the Unknown Unknowns", respectively, that the exploration of the unknown is an extremely important concept in realising the potential of any new instrument. This is especially true in an era of limited budgets but expanding analysis algorithms and capabilities. While this Chapter considers transients and environments, the ethos of these previous Chapters should be considered and embraced broadly and can be applied more broadly across SKAO science. We do not repeat in detail the important background these Chapters provide but encourage the reader to review them before reading this Chapter. In the last decade of radio transient astronomy, we have seen the value of these approaches with the expansion of the FRB population, the discovery of long period pulsars and transients and radio emission from white dwarfs to name just a few. With the SKAO, we should push the explored parameter space further and in new directions in all of the sensitivity, field-of-view, time, spectral, spectro-dynamic, polarisation and imaging domains. We should utilise approaches such as machine learning in allowing us to address the complexity that arises from the expanded parameter space and increased data rates and candidate sources. We will briefly summarise some of the impressive progress that the SKA pathfinders and precursors have made in these areas and what these mean for the SKA telescopes. We will also discuss ways in which it might be possible to push the current capabilities.

papers.title: Data-Driven Ages from Asteroseismology for FGK Dwarfs
papers.abstract: Age is the one of the most difficult stellar properties to constrain. However, upcoming surveys such as PLATO are about to revolutionize our ability to measure FGK dwarf ages with asteroseismology. Here, we use The Cannon to construct a data-driven model for inferring asteroseismic-quality age measurements from large spectroscopic survey observations and demonstrate that forthcoming asteroseismology datasets from future surveys can be leveraged, together with our model, to obtain stellar age samples larger than can be obtained by those surveys alone. We train The Cannon on 323 FGK dwarf stars with asteroseismic age labels from NASA Kepler photometry and high-resolution spectra from the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE). We apply our model to FGK dwarfs from the Kepler survey that exhibit solar-like oscillations and reproduce their reported asteroseismic-quality ages with an RMS scatter of 1.0 Gyr. We then apply our model to the sample of 3810 Kepler FGK dwarfs with APOGEE spectra to infer data-driven asteroseismic ages. We repeat this for the larger sample of 48,828 FGK dwarfs with APOGEE spectra. Our work demonstrates that data-driven methods can robustly reproduce asteroseismic ages for FGK dwarfs. These methods will be invaluable tools for extending asteroseimology measurements from upcoming surveys (e.g., PLATO) to much larger stellar samples.

papers.title: Coevolution of Dust Growth and Gravitational Instability in Massive Protostellar Disks
papers.abstract: Massive protostellar disks are expected to sustain high accretion rates through gravitational instability, while dust growth may modify their opacity, cooling efficiency, and stability. Conversely, the time-dependent and nonaxisymmetric structures produced by gravitational instability may regulate the local conditions for dust growth. However, the coupled evolution of dust growth and gravitational instability in massive protostellar disks has not yet been explored self-consistently. We present two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations that follow gas dynamics, dust growth, and opacity-dependent radiative cooling in a massive protostellar disk. We find that dust grains rapidly grow to millimeter-centimeter sizes shortly after disk formation, substantially reducing the infrared opacity. The enhanced cooling promotes disk fragmentation and produces more frequent accretion-driven luminosity outbursts than in a model without dust growth, with durations and peak luminosities comparable to those observed in massive protostars. Dust growth is broadly regulated by the fragmentation-limited size in dense disk regions, whereas newly formed outer disk regions and low-density regions deviate from this limit because of finite collision timescales and dust transport. These results suggest that dust growth may facilitate episodic accretion and fragmentation, while gravitationally unstable disk structures in turn regulate the dust growth process.

papers.title: Real-Time 24-hour Ahead Forecasting of Solar Energetic Particle Events with SEPNET-PRISM-R
papers.abstract: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events, operationally defined as proton flux exceeding 10 pfu in the >10 MeV channel, threaten spacecraft systems, astronaut safety, and high latitude aviation, yet continuous real-time forecasting with adequate lead time remains difficult. We present SEPNET-PRISM-R, a near-real-time system that issues hourly, 24 hour ahead probabilistic SEP forecasts. The model integrates multimodal solar data - including active region patches, flare features, coronal mass ejection (CME) characteristics, and historical proton flux - to concurrently predict SEP occurrences, peak proton flux, soft X-ray flux, and CME velocity, with the primary objective being SEP forecasting. Building on existing literature, SEPNET-PRISM-R enhances operational performance by incorporating a postprocessing module that enables cross-validated decision making and interpretable quantification of feature importance. The training dataset spans from February 1986 to September 2025, with subsequent forecasts generated sequentially through the present via a real-time space weather prediction platform that provides predictive probabilities, feature attributions, and historical analogs, enabling more reliable and informed operational decision-making. The proposed framework substantially suppresses false alarm rates while maintaining robust event detection capabilities, as evidenced by case studies and aggregate statistics.

papers.title: The Effect of Field Line Tracing Height on Wang-Sheeley-Arge Solar Wind Predictions at Earth
papers.abstract: (Abridged abstract): A key component of the widely used Wang-Sheeley-Arge model is the tracing of magnetic field lines in the solar corona, as that largely determines the modeled open/closed field regions and in turn the predicted large-scale solar wind structure. We demonstrate that by slightly raising the height from which magnetic field lines are traced from the photosphere (R$_{su}$), we can improve the prediction of solar wind high-speed enhancements (HSEs). We find a higher R$_{su}$ produces more accurate estimates of the HSE start time, duration, and peak speed, and enables the detection of HSEs that were missed with the standard R$_{su}$. These improvements are primarily associated with changes in the great-circle angular distance, while the flux tube expansion factors remain largely unchanged. A higher R$_{su}$ produces smoother open-field boundaries and reduces small-scale fragmentation within open-field regions. These morphological changes lead to more stable magnetic footpoint mappings and consequently more robust GCD calculations. To assess the statistical relevance of these findings, we extend the analysis to 53 Carrington rotations and perform a multi-metric evaluation of model performance. The results indicate that higher R$_{su}$ improves HSE predictions while reducing false alarms. We thus find that the choice of R$_{su}$ represents an important and previously underexplored parameter that can help enhance our ambient solar wind modeling and forecasting capabilities.

papers.title: $Z_3$ and $S_3$ gaugings of $Z_NZ'_N$ non-invertible symmetries: quark texture zeros and phenomenology
papers.abstract: We investigate texture zeros in the quark Yukawa matrices arising from the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $S_3$ gauging of $\mathbb{Z}_N\times\mathbb{Z}'_N$, associated with the non-invertible $\Delta(3N^2)$ and $\Delta(6N^2)$ symmetries, respectively. We construct the equivalence classes and their fusion rules and use them as selection rules for the Yukawa interactions. We systematically classify the full-rank quark Yukawa textures generated by the two gaugings for $N=2,3,4,$ and $5$. The two gaugings yield the same texture spectrum for $N=2$ and $N=4$, whereas the $S_3$ gauging produces additional textures for $N=3$ and $N=5$. We further analyze the most restrictive texture pairs compatible with quark data and find that there are at most nine zeros in these texture pairs. For up- and down-quark mass matrices with a total of nine texture zeros, one sector is allowed to contain six zeros while the other contains three, or one contains five zeros while the other contains four. The former case has been studied in previous works. We perform numerical fits for the latter and find it consistent with experimental data. Some viable textures also admit real quark-mass determinants while retaining a physical CKM phase, suggesting a possible connection to the strong CP problem.

papers.title: Orbital Parameters for 65 Wide Binary Systems: no evidence for gravitational anomaly at low acceleration
papers.abstract: We use a Monte Carlo analysis to study whether wide binaries can be represented by bound Newtonian orbits, and, if this is the case, whether the distribution of the orbital parameters agrees with expectations. The potential orbits are classified according to the $\chi^2$ probability of representing star coordinates, parallaxes, velocity components and masses. We apply this analysis to 44 systems previously published, to which we add 26 wide binaries, consisting of twin low-mass (M) stars. We find orbital solutions for 65 systems, and derive the distribution of their orbital parameters. For one system composed of M-type stars, no Newtonian bound solution can be found; however, this pair is a member of the young Argus association and therefore not a suitable target. The remaining four systems that cannot be fit were already identified as likely disrupted binaries. The uncertainty in the separation between the components, given by the parallax error, is by far the dominant error source, and the main limitation of the present analysis, affecting especially the determination of the orbits' inclination angle and phase. Newtonian dynamics describe well our sample. When dividing the sample into two subsamples, according to the mutual acceleration, the eccentricity and periastron distributions agree with theoretical expectations; inclination and phase are distorted by the parallax-limited separation, more strongly in the high-acceleration (37 systems) than in the low-acceleration ($A_N < 10^{-9} m s^{-2}$, 28 systems) subsample, which is opposite to what a gravitational signal would produce. In particular the ratio between observed velocity difference and circular velocity does not show any excess for the low acceleration sample. When parametrized as a boost $\gamma$ parameter to the velocity, $0.95 < \gamma <1.05 (1 \sigma)$, fully consistent with Newton also for the low acceleration sample.

papers.title: Hadronization in QCD and Fragmentation Functions
papers.abstract: The hadronization of quarks and gluons is reviewed within the framework of collinear parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions closely associated with the notion of factorization in hard scattering processes in QCD. The state-of-the-art in calculating both the scale evolution of fragmentation functions and the partonic cross sections pertinent to their determination from data up to next-to-next-to-leading order accuracy is presented. Potential improvements up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic order are outlined as well. All relevant experimental data sets for single-inclusive pion, kaon, and unidentified charged hadron production are listed. The most recent sets of fragmentation functions and their uncertainties extracted from these data in global QCD analyses utilizing various different strategies are presented and compared to each other.

papers.title: Soft Breaking Naturalness in Majorana Fermion Loop induced Scalar and Majoron Amplitudes
papers.abstract: Majorana fermion loops contribute a shift-symmetry violating effective potential to the coupled scalar field. When the Majorana fermion is light, a larger number of symmetry violating insertions let the loop contribution to grow increasingly infrared sensitive to the Majorana mass. With explicit calculations, we calculate the symmetry violating amplitudes, show that the scalar potential's natural scales serve as nonzero kinematic matching points which remove the superficial sensitivity to the symmetry-violating Majorana mass, continuously restoring the shift symmetry in agreement with 't Hooft naturalness. In the spontaneous broken phase, the scalar radial vacuum expectation value readily ensures the infrared safety of symmetry violating Majorana fermion loops, and all $n$-point Majoron functions develop a leading linear dependence on the symmetry violating parameter in the soft breaking limit, which matches the expansion of the Coleman-Weinberg determinant.

papers.title: Finite Spectral Recurrences for Loop Integrals in de Sitter and Anti-de Sitter Space
papers.abstract: We introduce a method that does for loop integrals in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter space what integration-by-parts identities do in flat space. A local, coordinate-free propagator algebra common to both geometries yields exact finite-difference equations in spectral labels; with external points they become differential-difference equations, and at the AdS boundary recover known Witten-diagram relations. Acting line by line, they apply in principle to any diagram. We solve them for the two-loop watermelon, isolating its ultraviolet poles, and for one-loop two- and four-point functions.

papers.title: Hidden engines in tidal disruption events: multimessenger signatures in a lepto-hadronic framework
papers.abstract: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) provide a unique laboratory for studying transient accretion, outflows, particle acceleration, and the possible connection between stellar disruptions and high-energy neutrinos. Motivated by recent candidate TDE-neutrino associations and by the forthcoming sensitivity of multimessenger facilities, we investigate under which physical conditions TDEs can be detected in MeV, GeV, and TeV gamma rays, and in high-energy neutrinos. We develop a lepto-hadronic emission framework and apply it to three representative sources: AT2019dsg, AT2019ehz, and ASASSN-14li. For each source we explore a set of physically motivated models that vary the proton and electron spectral indices, the minimum Lorentz factor of non-thermal protons, the particle energy partition, the acceleration efficiency, the magnetic compactness, and the presence of a compact corona. We compute the broadband spectral energy distributions, the associated muon-neutrino spectra, and compare them with reference sensitivities for COSI, Fermi/LAT, CTAO, and KM3NeT/ARCA. We find that hard proton spectra and/or large minimum proton Lorentz factors are the most favourable conditions for TeV gamma-ray and neutrino detectability, while GeV-bright models can be predominantly leptonic and neutrino quiet. AT2019dsg and AT2019ehz can reach the CTAO and KM3NeT benchmarks in hadronically favourable configurations, whereas ASASSN-14li is more naturally bright in the MeV-GeV band and constrained by its radio synchrotron emission. Our results highlight the importance of combining MeV, GeV, TeV, radio, and neutrino observations to distinguish between transparent, hidden, and lepton-dominated TDE emission regimes.

papers.title: Polarization signatures of mixed scalar - pseudoscalar ALP - photon couplings in intense laser pulses
papers.abstract: We investigate photon-to-axion-like-particle (ALP) conversion in a finite, linearly polarized laser pulse for a single ALP field with simultaneous scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type couplings to photons. Varying the collision angle between the strong pulse and the probe provides a continuous kinematic scan of the resonant ALP mass. For fixed kinematics in this setting, the scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type ALP conversion amplitudes interfere coherently, making both the photon-to-ALP conversion probability and the polarization rotation depend on the difference between the probe polarization angle $\alpha$ and the coupling angle $\theta_g$. Conversion is maximal at $|\alpha-\theta_g|=90^\circ$, where the polarization rotation vanishes, while the rotation magnitude peaks at $\alpha-\theta_g=45^\circ$ modulo $90^\circ$, where conversion is half-maximal. These complementary polarization-angle dependences provide polarization-resolved signatures of mixed scalar--pseudoscalar photon couplings.

papers.title: A Catalog of Lepton Mass Textures from Koide and Alikhanov Relations
papers.abstract: The empirical Koide relation for charged-lepton masses and the recently proposed Alikhanov relation for neutrino mass-squared differences offer intriguing hints toward understanding the structure of lepton mass matrices. Motivated by these observations, we systematically explore charged-lepton and neutrino mass-matrix textures that satisfy these relations and confront their predictions for lepton mixing with experimental data. For the charged-lepton sector, we investigate representative positive Hermitian square-root matrices classified by the number of common eigenvector directions of their generators: three, one, or none. For the neutrino sector, an exhaustive enumeration of real symmetric integer matrices with entries between $-5$ and $5$ identifies six signed-permutation classes with $m_1=0$ and six with $m_1>0$ that satisfy the Alikhanov relation. Combining these neutrino textures with the charged-lepton constructions, allowing for different relative flavor orientations and phase alignments, yields $400$ viable structural pairs consistent with the measured lepton mixing parameters. All retained solutions satisfy the adopted cosmological bound on the sum of neutrino masses and existing laboratory constraints. In particular, the full-rank neutrino textures predict $m_1\simeq16.77$-$17.22\,\mathrm{meV}$. Representative viable solutions yield effective Majorana masses $m_{\beta\beta}\simeq1.29$-$4.03\,\mathrm{meV}$ and $4.07$-$18.67\,\mathrm{meV}$ for the $m_1=0$ and $m_1>0$ branches, respectively, providing potential targets for future high-sensitivity searches.

papers.title: On the Stability of Tolman Oppenheimer Volkoff Fireholes
papers.abstract: We investigate the radial stability of singular Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff fireholes with a radiation equation of state. These configurations contain a naked, negative point-mass singularity surrounded by a positive-density fluid, whose mass profile develops a Schwarzschild-like plateau before approaching an extended, self-similar atmosphere. Using the Pr\"ufer phase method to identify the fundamental radial mode, we consider two outer boundary conditions: vanishing Lagrangian pressure perturbation (open firehole) and vanishing radial displacement (boxed firehole). For both, the fundamental squared frequency changes from positive to negative as the outer boundary exceeds a critical radius $R_c$. We find that $R_c$ follows approximately the same scaling with the central mass parameter as the equilibrium firehole radius $R$. However, the stability thresholds differ significantly: $R_c^{\rm O}<R$ for the open firehole, whereas $R_c^{\rm B}\simeq R$ for the boxed one. The regular zero mode is the derivative of the equilibrium family with respect to the inner lapse normalization at fixed central mass. This gives the boxed threshold a turning-point interpretation and, together with a scaling symmetry of the TOV equations, implies $R_c^{\rm B}\to R$ in the limit of large central mass. Variational bounds show that the rigid wall is the most stabilizing separated, self-adjoint outer boundary condition and that the unbounded configuration is unstable. Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff fireholes are therefore radially unstable unless confined within approximately their firehole radius.

papers.title: Detection and Statistics of large-scale Sector Boundary Crossings in the Solar Wind: The SBCross Catalog
papers.abstract: Heliospheric sector boundary crossings (SBCs), composed of the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS), Heliospheric Plasma Sheet (HPS), and surrounding plasma halo, represent fundamental structures in the solar wind that influence interplanetary dynamics and space weather. We present the \textsc{SBCross} catalog, an automated, publicly available database containing 1,076 SBC events derived from in-situ observations spanning more than 30 years (1995--2026), covering Solar Cycles 23 and 24 alongside the rising and maximum phases of Solar Cycle 25. By combining interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) and 255~eV suprathermal electron pitch angle distributions (PAD) data, our algorithm reliably captures large-scale polarity transitions, with $76\%$ of detected SBCs exhibiting clear HPS signatures ($\beta > 1$, $n_{\mathrm{peak}} > 10\mathrm{\,cm^{-3}}$). Across the catalog, we find an average occurrence rate of $\approx 2.6$ events per Carrington rotation, a median event duration of $\approx 9.0$\,hours, and a median physical thickness of $\approx 7.4 \times 10^6$\,km. Furthermore, approximately $\approx 15\%$ of detected SBCs interact with interplanetary coronal mass ejections (CMEs) on average, with this proportion rising up to $33\%$ during solar maximum. These CME-associated events exhibit systematically longer durations (median of $10.0$\,hours), $54\%$ larger physical thicknesses, and higher average solar wind velocities. Notably, all high-velocity SBC events ($> 600\mathrm{\,km\,s^{-1}}$) are exclusively driven by CME interactions, demonstrating local plasma pile-up and structural entanglement resulting from fast CMEs overtaking the ambient slow background. The \textsc{SBCross} catalog serves as an updated successor to the classic SBC list by L. Svalgaard, delivering a standardized, open-access resource for the heliophysics community to systematically investigate sector boundary transitions.

papers.title: Form factors and weak decays of $_b_c^*(2595)$ and $_b_c^*(2790)$
Deriving Interplanetary Sector Boundary Crossings using Potential Field Source Surface Modeling
papers.abstract: The Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS) and associated interplanetary sector boundaries fundamentally structure the solar wind environment, modulating coronal mass ejection (CME) evolution and solar energetic particle transport. In this study, we evaluate the capability of a static Potential Field Source Surface (PFSS; $R_{ss}=2.5R_\odot$) coronal model to directly map interplanetary sector boundary crossings from the Sun to 1 au without dynamic heliospheric propagation models. We compare ballistically transported HCS crossings derived from GONG-ADAPT and SDO/HMI magnetic maps against sector boundary crossing observations from the SBCross catalog. PFSS modeling reproduces the large-scale interplanetary magnetic field topology well ($J\approx0.50$), achieving hit rates (POD) of 0.64 for GONG-ADAPT and 0.76 for HMI. Carrington synoptic maps outperform flux-transport modeled maps, suggesting that the short-term observational noise from data assimilation degrades topological matching more than map "aging". Predictive skill shows a strong solar cycle dependence, performing significantly better during solar maxima (POD=0.70-0.81) than solar minima (POD=0.56-0.67), attributed to more distinct crossings due to higher HCS inclination angles during maximum. Matched events exhibit travel times close to ballistic estimates of 4.8-4.9 days with an average timing difference centered near zero ($\pm1.1$ days) and 90% of events within $\pm 1.8$ days. The hit rate of HCS structures that interact with CMEs does not degrade (POD = 0.67-0.83), despite propagating $\approx7$ hours faster on average, implying that the CME interaction causes only minor structural changes to the HCS. Larger timing differences (>24 hours) are associated with flatter current sheets. Overall, static PFSS extrapolations offer a computationally inexpensive, effective approach for mapping global sector boundary structure.

papers.title: The T-matrix method for modeling the optical properties of grains in exoplanetary atmospheres
papers.abstract: Observations of exoplanetary atmospheres have revealed a rather complex co-existence between the gaseous and condensed phases, ranging from atmospheres apparently covered in clouds to clear ones, across a myriad of intermediate regimes. The interaction between solids and stellar radiation is of fundamental importance when forward or retrieval models are compared to observations. The simplest approach is to assume spherical particles, whose scattering and absorption properties are readily computed with Mie theory. More advanced computational methods, however, can also treat non-spherical condensates. Among these, the transition matrix approach has proven to provide a rigorous and efficient calculation of the extinction by non-spherical particles over a broad range of sizes and refractive indices. We here focus on the absorption and scattering cross sections of forsterite, spinel and silicon monoxide from the near to the far infrared range for particles of different sizes, with shapes ranging from compact ensembles of spheres to porous aggregates. We find that, depending on the size and the configuration chosen, the differences in extinction can be as high as a factor of 2-3, with structured grains being more efficient absorbers in the near infrared for sizes greater than 1 $\mu$m. In a fiducial transmission spectrum we show that in the $\lambda = 1-5\,\mu$m range the amount of spherical material needed to match the contribution of the structured grains can be a factor 2 higher. Such calculations, available for the community through a Zenodo repository, prove to be useful for interpreting recent and future observations of exoplanetary atmospheres.

papers.title: Information geometry of DGLAP evolution
papers.abstract: Quark and gluon splittings shift proton momentum toward smaller fractions with increasing resolution. Momentum conservation makes the summed momentum-weighted quark and gluon densities, when nonnegative, a probability distribution. We apply information geometry, the geometry of probability distributions, to this probabilistic form of Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi evolution. We evaluate, to our knowledge for the first time, the speed at which the shape of the proton's momentum distribution changes, measured by how well distributions at neighboring resolutions can be told apart statistically. At leading order, with one-loop splitting functions and running coupling, five fixed quark flavors, nonnegative quark and gluon densities and sufficiently regular inputs, we obtain a closed-form lower bound on this speed. Once the coupling is specified, three numbers of the input (the distribution at the starting resolution) fix the bound at every scale without computing the evolved distribution. For three of the five model inputs at four scales from 2 GeV to 10 TeV, the squared bound is at least 94.8 percent of the squared speed. The bound is reached when the distribution's relative rate of change is linear in the logarithm of the inverse momentum fraction. For these three model inputs at the four scales, the relative rate of change is close to this linear form in mean square weighted by momentum.

papers.title: Thin-Shell Wormholes in Born--Infeld-Type Magnetic Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We investigate the radial stability, thermodynamic balance, and bilateral disk images of symmetric thin-shell wormholes built from Born--Infeld-type magnetic exteriors. The exact lapse and junction conditions define a fixed-mass family in which magnetic self-energy ties the nonlinear scale to the charge. The shell has negative energy density, although an inner sampled region satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. Linear radial perturbations yield unstable calibrated barotropic samples and stable sectors for the generalized and modified cosmic Chaplygin laws on selected real branches. Analytic horizon and large-radius limits explain the stability transitions and show how the modified linear pressure term can replace outer stability with finite radial intervals. Minimally coupled Maxwell rays traverse transparent junctions between exteriors with a common arctangent emission profile, viewed by a static observer. The wormhole-black-hole intensity difference separates transmitted disk light from emission removed by throat excision. Compared with static emitters, circular and plunging motion reduce the face-on intensities in the studied cases; inclined motion generates strong azimuthal contrast. Increasing the subcritical charge contracts the critical circle and permits more disk crossings near it in the optical samples. Under a reversible first law, flux cancellation gives isentropic motion at positive temperature, with entropy dependence left to a constitutive completion. These results distinguish geometric, material, and kinematic effects on shell support and disk illumination.

papers.title: Pulsar J1909+0749 and Supernova Remnant G42.1-0.2: A case of a pulsar that has exited the shell of its associated supernova remnant
papers.abstract: (Abridged) The ATNF pulsar catalogue features only 63 pulsars that are possibly associated with a supernova remnant (SNR). Even rarer is the scenario in which the pulsar has escaped the physical extent of its corresponding SNR. We aim to identify the serendipitously discovered shell-type object G42.1-0.2 as a SNR. The known pulsar (PSR) J1909+0749 lies well outside the shell of SNR G42.1-0.2, but it has a cometary tail pointing towards the centre of the SNR; we propose that the SNR and the pulsar originated from the same supernova explosion. By measuring the flux densities of the shell G42.1-0.2 from ${\sim}$200 MHz to ${\sim}$6 GHz, we establish the nonthermal nature of its emission. With the characteristic age of the pulsar, its distance from the Sun estimated from the dispersion measure (DM), and the angular separation between the pulsar and the centre of the shell, we infer the evolutionary state of the SNR and the transverse velocity of the pulsar. Using proper motion measurements, we compare the SNR-pulsar direction with the velocity of the pulsar. The radio spectral index of the shell is $-0.36 \pm 0.08$, confirming that the emission is primarily nonthermal synchrotron. The proper motion measurements are not well constrained, but the amplitude and the direction are consistent with the interpretation that the SNR and the pulsar are associated. If the characteristic age and the DM-based distance represent the true age and the true distance of the pulsar and the SNR, then the standard evolution equations suggest that the SNR must still be in the Sedov-Taylor phase, evolving in a medium with a density of about 1.5 cm$^{-3}$. In addition, as a result of the PSR-SNR association, the transverse velocity of the pulsar PSR J1909+0749 is estimated to be ${\sim}1460~\mathrm{km\,s}^{-1}$, ranking it among the highest transverse velocities observed for pulsars in the Milky Way.

papers.title: Constraints on Dark Matter Annihilation from Starlight-Induced Inverse Compton Emission in Omega Centauri
papers.abstract: The search for the particle identity of dark matter (DM) remains one of the foremost challenges in modern physics. In this work, we derive new constraints on the DM annihilation cross section $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ by considering the inverse Compton (IC) scattering of DM annihilation injected $e^+e^-$ off the starlight radiation field in Omega Centauri. As a likely remnant core of a dwarf galaxy, Omega Centauri provides a dense stellar environment that enhances the predict IC signal. Using multi-wavelength observations from Chandra and Fermi-LAT, we establish upper limits on $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ over a wide DM mass range from MeV to TeV. Notably, in the tens-of-MeV range, our results surpass existing constraints by approximately two orders of magnitude, exceeding $\langle\sigma v\rangle \sim 10^{-31}~{\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At several GeV to the TeV DM masses range, our constraints also remain stronger than existing limits. Our results demonstrate that starlight induced IC emission is an important component for indirect DM searches in dense stellar systems, establishing Omega Centauri as a powerful probe of the nature of DM.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Goldberg-Palatini Action from Noether Identities
papers.abstract: We investigate the reconstruction of the first-order gravitational action from the Noether identities associated with diffeomorphism invariance. The independent fields are a symmetric perturbation $\phi^{\mu\nu}$ of the contravariant metric density and a trace-adjusted connection $G^{\lambda}{}_{\mu\nu}$, whose transformation laws are prescribed. For a local action polynomial in these fields, with the gravitational coupling as its only dimensionful constant and each additional field carrying one power of it, a dilatation, which is a particular diffeomorphism, shows that in any dimension $d>2$ the action terminates at most at cubic order, its only possible cubic term being a derivative-free $\phi GG$ vertex. Expanding the kernels of the resulting Lorentz-covariant ansatz in tensor bases gives 31 coefficients for $d\geq 4$. The Noether identities with general diffeomorphisms, expanded order by order in the fields, yield a linear system that eliminates the $\phi\phi$ kernel and determines the remaining coefficients up to an overall normalization, recovering the Goldberg-Palatini action. Since the connection can be eliminated exactly, this also fixes the complete second-order action, with its infinite set of graviton vertices. The construction requires no choice of energy-momentum tensor, the source of ambiguity in the self-coupling approach. The kernel bases, the identities and the solution are given in appendices, and the symbolic computations are publicly available.

papers.title: Time-Reversal Symmetry in Artificial Topological Graphene Rings
papers.abstract: We study an artificial graphene ring described by the low-energy two-valley Dirac Hamiltonian with a uniform mass term. When the ring is threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, the problem reduces to a second-order radial equation solved by Bessel functions. We give the exact secular equation and, for narrow rings, closed expressions for the spectrum and the persistent current. We then add a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane. The radial problem is solved with confluent hypergeometric functions, and the persistent current and magnetization are written as derivatives of a secular determinant from which the spurious roots have been removed. Besides the usual orbital coupling, the field enters through a valley-dependent term that comes from the Dirac structure and lifts the valley degeneracy. A weak-field expansion, accurate up to corrections of order B^4, gives this valley splitting explicitly and separates the diamagnetic and paramagnetic contributions to the susceptibility. Finally, we work out what time reversal implies for the spectrum. Physical time reversal, which exchanges the valleys, leads to an exact relation between levels at opposite fields. The effective single-valley time reversal, on the other hand, is broken by the mass term and by the boundary conditions, yet leaves no trace in the zero-field spectrum. Numerical results for the spectrum, the persistent current, and the magnetization illustrate the analysis.

papers.title: On the superbursts as photodisintegrators of ashes from the rp-process -- Numerical simulations of superbursts with MESA II
papers.abstract: Context: Superbursts are energetic explosions in the crusts of neutron stars in Low-Mass X-ray Binaries (LMXBs). At temperatures above 4 GK, photodisintegration of heavy rp-process ashes may play a major role alongside $^{12}$C fusion. Aims: We investigate how photodisintegration of rp-process ashes affects superburst properties and the initial $^{12}$C abundance required for ignition. Methods: We simulate superbursts with MESA v.24.08.1. Besides the canonical fuel of $20\%$ $^{12}$C and $80\%$ $^{56}$Fe, we test different $^{12}$C abundances mixed with scaled rp-process ashes. Results: Superbursts can ignite with only $10\%$ $^{12}$C when the remaining $90\%$ consists of rp-process ashes. Their luminosity is comparable to that of the canonical fuel, whereas $10\%$ $^{12}$C mixed with $90\%$ $^{56}$Fe yields lower luminosity. $^{56}$Fe remains the most abundant ash nuclide. Although photodisintegration drives nucleosynthesis, neutron, proton and alpha captures release energy at late times. We also find that $A=64$ nuclides or $^{20}$Ne help reduce the $^{12}$C abundance needed for ignition. Conclusions: The composition of accreted material - not just its $^{12}$C content - substantially affects superburst ignition, luminosity and nucleosynthesis.

papers.title: Rapid Variability of Radiative Signatures from Driven Relativistic Reconnection
papers.abstract: Rapid variability in energetic flares is a distinctive feature of high-energy emission from many magnetically dominated astrophysical sources. We investigate the radiative variability of driven relativistic magnetic reconnection using Particle-in-Cell simulations of strongly magnetized flux tubes pushed to merge at driving speed $v_{\rm push}$. This setup captures the onset of reconnection and provides a controlled model for single reconnection-driven flares near compact objects, where magnetic structures can be twisted, sheared, and forced to merge by turbulent accretion flows or relativistic frame dragging. We find that the merger efficiently accelerates particles into nonthermal distributions, producing synchrotron emission whose variability tracks the reconnection phases. We identify two regimes: a quasi-steady, weakly driven regime for $v_{push}\leq0.1\,c$, and strongly driven regime for $v_{\rm push}>0.1\,c$. The transition occurs when the driving exceeds the typical inflow-to-outflow velocity ratio of $\sim0.1$ in steady collisionless relativistic reconnection, i.e., the average rate at which reconnection can process incoming flux, potentially providing an additional source of variability. The lightcurves rise on $1$--$3$ light-crossing times of the reconnecting region, and the particle spectra develop power laws with index $p\simeq1.8$--$2.4$. These timescales are compatible with observed variability in high-energy sources, including the very-high-energy flares of M87$^*$ and the $\gamma$-ray flares of the Crab Nebula, making this model a viable framework for rapid flaring in active galactic nuclei and pulsar wind nebulae.

papers.title: Direct Urca process facilitated by non-Fermi-liquid quantum criticality
papers.abstract: Conventional Fermi-liquid theories of dense nuclear matter predict that the direct Urca process requires a proton fraction above a threshold of $Y_p \approx 0.11$--$0.15$, which is rarely reached in low-mass neutron stars. Here we show that this stringent kinematic constraint is drastically relaxed by the non-Fermi liquid behavior arising from superfluid and superconducting quantum criticality in neutron stars. In the non-Fermi-liquid regimes, nucleons have a smooth momentum occupation without a sharp Fermi surface, and their chemical potentials develop a logarithmic temperature dependence. These intrinsic features fundamentally alter the standard $\beta$-equilibrium relation. Consequently, direct Urca neutrino emission can be activated even at low nuclear densities. This modifies the long-standing Urca-threshold paradigm and indicates that direct Urca process has the opportunity to occur in low-mass neutron stars.

papers.title: Femtoscopic correlation functions between the lightest charmed hadrons
papers.abstract: Femtoscopic momentum correlations probe low-energy interactions of short-lived charmed hadrons that are inaccessible to conventional scattering experiments. We calculate the correlation functions of $D^{+}D^{+}$, $D^{0}D^{0}$, $D^{+}D^{0}$, and $\Lambda_c^+\Lambda_c^+$ in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02$~TeV, using species-dependent non-Gaussian PHSD sources constructed from hadronization points and strong interactions calibrated to lattice-QCD scattering lengths: OBE and EFT-contact models for $DD$, and an EFT-contact model for $\Lambda_c\Lambda_c$. Coulomb and quantum-statistical effects are included consistently. Although the calibrated interactions are weakly repulsive, the channels separate the relevant effects: $D^{+}D^{0}$, free of Coulomb distortion and identical-particle interference, gives the cleanest access to the $DD$ strong interaction, whereas $\Lambda_c^+\Lambda_c^+$ is most pronounced in peripheral collisions, where the compact source enhances the low-momentum signal. The $\Lambda_c\Lambda_c$ input is taken from lattice QCD at a nonphysical pion mass, so its physical-point shift is not quantified here. Within these stated inputs, the results provide ALICE-ready benchmark correlations and background references; the quoted bands propagate only the lattice scattering-length uncertainty.

papers.title: Relativistic Strong Quantum Mpemba Effect
papers.abstract: The Unruh effect links acceleration to thermalization, providing a relativistic setting for anomalous quantum relaxation. We demonstrate a {\it relativistic} strong quantum Mpemba effect in the Unruh thermalization of a two-level detector coupled to a massless scalar field. For a fixed pair of isospectral initial states, relaxation curves that never cross in inertial motion exhibit a Mpemba crossing above a threshold acceleration. At a higher, precisely tuned acceleration, the initially farther state has zero overlap with the slowest decay mode and relaxes with a faster asymptotic exponential rate. We identify how competition between transition and dephasing channels governs the relaxation spectrum, where sufficiently strong longitudinal coupling enables acceleration to switch the relaxation bottleneck between population and coherence modes. We derive the spectral-switching condition and construct isospectral preparation protocols that eliminate slow-mode contributions within their physical domains. These protocols reveal how coherence can suppress or enhance slow-mode overlap at fixed purity, depending on the underlying spectral structure. Our results establish acceleration as a control parameter for anomalous quantum relaxation, connecting relativistic quantum dynamics with nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

papers.title: Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition via a Two-Step Mechanism in the Inert Doublet plus Real Singlet Model
papers.abstract: We study a two-component dark matter model in which a real singlet scalar and an inert doublet scalar are simultaneously present alongside the Standard Model, each stabilized by an independent discrete symmetry. The real singlet undergoes a strong first-order transition at high temperature, establishing an intermediate phase with a non-zero singlet vacuum expectation value, which in turn generates the barrier required for the Higgs field to complete a strongly first-order electroweak transition at a lower temperature. This two-step mechanism naturally enforces the condition $v_c/T_c \geq 1$, the sphaleron washout-avoidance criterion necessary for electroweak baryogenesis. The gravitational wave spectrum from both steps is computed; the second step produces a decihertz signal, peaking near $0.08$--$0.34~\mathrm{Hz}$ across the viable parameter space and $0.14$--$0.22~\mathrm{Hz}$ at the benchmark points, that reaches the sensitivity of DECIGO for the strongest transitions and of BBO more widely, while the first remains sub-threshold for all planned detectors. At the coupling values required to drive the phase transition, the singlet is generically underabundant as a thermal relic, so the inert doublet carries the dominant fraction of the observed relic density. Confronting the model with current constraints, we find that the LUX-ZEPLIN 2024 result excludes the entire electroweak-phase-transition-viable parameter space of the singlet sector across the full mass range, even after rescaling by the singlet relic fraction, establishing a complete no-go for the singlet as a viable thermal dark matter candidate in this framework.

papers.title: Kinematically isolating intracluster light in AS1063: a distinct stellar population tracing the dark matter core
papers.abstract: We present a technique using integral-field spectroscopy to kinematically isolate intracluster light (ICL) from the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG), enabling insights into their contrasting stellar populations and the inner dark matter halo profile. Applying this technique to MUSE data of Abell S1063, we find that both components are old (~9 Gyr), but the ICL is more metal-poor than the BCG, implying distinct progenitor pathways. Within 100 kpc, the ICL comprises 55 per cent of the BCG+ICL stellar mass - substantially more than inferred from photometric decompositions. The BCG and ICL possess distinct velocity distributions, which remain nearly constant with radius, with an ICL velocity dispersion more than twice that of the BCG, and a line-of-sight velocity offset of 86 +- 18 km/s. Two-dimensional S\'ersic fits yield an ICL centroid offset of 5.2 +- 1.5 kpc from the BCG. These phase-space offsets are indicative of the BCG oscillating in a broad potential minimum. Furthermore, the ICL surface-brightness profile matches that of strong-lensing estimates assuming a cored halo. Simulations indicate that the inner halo profile varies systematically for different dark matter models. Applied to larger samples, our method therefore offers a complementary route to testing the nature of dark matter, while simultaneously revealing the stellar origins of the ICL.

papers.title: An improvement to the spatial discretisation in the Astrophysical Weighted Particle Hydrodynamics method
papers.abstract: The discretisation of space in the Astrophysical Weighted Particle Hydrodynamics method is attained through a partition-of-unity-based cubature rule. The node (particle) weights in such rules must in general be obtained using approximations, for which only one has been thus far proposed in the literature. In this work, new approximations for these weights are proposed, their properties are studied, and their impact on the accuracy of the cubature rule and the overall method is assessed. Approximations for node centroids are also proposed and studied, and their possible applications are laid out. Additionally, for schemes in which the kernel-function compact-support size is set to be constant, rather than adaptive, weight and centroid approximations are provided as well. Finally, for the cubature rule arising from the weight approximation previously proposed in the literature, an asymptotic expression for its mean relative error is derived, and its usefulness for understanding the finite-sample properties of the cubature rule is showcased with some simple examples.
